title: SLO Ledger and Capacity Escrow Playbook
author: Priya Nair
content:
Overview

Purpose
This playbook defines the SLO Ledger and Capacity Escrow model we use to reconcile transient SLO deficits with finite capacity resources. The goal is to provide a predictable, auditable, and automatable process to:
- Capture SLO burn events and assign capacity credits.
- Maintain an immutable ledger of allocations, amortization schedules, and expirations.
- Enable safe capacity swaps and temporary credit issuance to prevent cascading degradation.

Scope
Applies to all production model-serving services managed by eng-sre and runtime teams. This includes Hosted API, Dedicated clusters, and Private deployments where Redwood controls capacity. For customer-managed on-prem deployments, adapt the principles and local tooling.

Definitions
- SLO ledger entry: immutable record representing a discrete SLO event, required capacity, timestamps, and assigned credits.
- Capacity escrow: a logical pool of capacity credits reserved (escrowed) to be used against ledgered SLO deficits.
- Credit amortization: gradual application of escrowed credits over a reconciliation window to smooth traffic and cost impact.
- Debt window: the maximum time an SLO deficit may be carried against the ledger before requiring governance escalation. Default: 14 days.

Principles
- All allocations must be auditable with owner, rationale, and TTL.
- Use escrow conservatively: prefer autoscale and routing fallbacks before consuming credits.
- Short lived amortization is preferred to long-term debt.
- Automation first: human approval only for exceptions outside policy.

SLO Ledger Model (conceptual)
Each ledger entry contains these attributes (text-only representation):
- id: unique UUID
- service: e.g., text-generation-prod-v2
- slo_name: p50_latency_ms / availability_99.9
- observed_window: 10m / 1h / 7d
- deficit: numeric units (tokens/sec capacity shortfall or error-rate delta)
- credits_required: integer (capacity units)
- assigned_escrow_id: escrow pool UUID or null
- amortization_policy: immediate|linear|frontloaded
- ttl: ISO timestamp when entry expires
- owner: oncall alias or SRE steward
- reason: short description and incident link

Example ledger entry (JSON shown as an example string in the UI):
{
  "id": "ledg-1f3a9b",
  "service": "text-generation-prod-v2",
  "slo_name": "availability_99.9",
  "observed_window": "1h",
  "deficit": "0.25%",
  "credits_required": "20-gpu-steps",
  "assigned_escrow_id": "escrow-81a2",
  "amortization_policy": "linear-6h",
  "ttl": "2026-02-21T13:00:00Z",
  "owner": "oncall-textgen",
  "reason": "Canary rollout caused tail latency spikes, incident-2026-02-15-4"
}

Capacity Escrow Pools
We maintain named escrow pools with allocation policies and owners. Pools are logical, backed by capacity reservations or burst credits:
- pool_id: escrow-81a2
- name: safety-burst-east-1
- owner_team: eng-sre-capacity
- total_credits: 500-gpu-steps
- reserved_for: critical-slos, can be limited per tenant
- replenishment: manual | automated (policy)

Example pools and recommended use cases
- safety-burst-global: for emergency cross-region failover and global tier SLOs.
- tenant-escrow: dedicated per-large-customer for contractual remediation.
- experiment-credits: short TTL credits used for canary ramping.

Operational Procedures
1) Detection and Ledger Entry Creation (automated)
- Trigger: alert rule detects SLO burn rate > threshold or a validated postmortem flags an ongoing deficit.
- Action: automation creates ledger entry with observed metrics and suggested credits.
- Tooling: SLO-observer service writes to ledger API: `redwood ledger create --service $S --slo $SLO --deficit $D --owner $ONCALL --reason "$SUMMARY"`

2) Escrow Assignment (automated preferred)
- Policy evaluation determines if a pool matches the SLO type, region, and tenant.
- If matching pool has capacity, ledger entry is assigned and amortization policy chosen.
- If no pool available, escalate to capacity steward and apply fallback routing policies.

3) Amortization and Application
- Credits are applied per the amortization policy (e.g., linear-6h applies 1/6th of credits every hour).
- System emits synthetic traffic-shift events and records actual SLO progress.
- If SLO improves ahead of schedule, remaining credits are released back to the pool (pro-rated).

4) Reconciliation Cadence
- Daily automatic reconciliation job evaluates open ledger entries and pool balances.
- Weekly review meeting (SLO veterans + capacity) for anything older than 72 hours.
- Governance escalation if ledger entries reach debt window or exceed pool policy limits.

5) Expiry and Audit
- On TTL expiry, unused credits are returned to pool and entry is flagged closed.
- All actions produce signed audit events: who/what/when/why. Audit logs are retained 1 year by default.

Governance and Escalation
- Minor: single ledger entry < 10% of pool and < 24h TTL — auto-approved.
- Major: entry requiring > 25% of pool or > 14 days TTL — requires Capacity Council approval.
- Emergency: cross-region outage; immediate pool reallocation possible with oncall+incident commander signoff.

SLO-to-Capacity Mapping Guidelines
- Latency deficits: map to additional gpu-steps or shard count based on historical serving profiles.
- Availability deficits: map to redundancy or region failover credits.
- Embedding throughput: map to batch slots or large-host ephemeral credits.

Mapping example (text-generation-prod-v2)
- 10% p99 tail latency increase for 30m => estimated 10 gpu-steps for 2h (staging amortization: linear-2h)
- 0.2% availability drop for 1h => failover credits: 2 region-replicas for 1h

Tooling Integration (examples)
- Prometheus alert rule snippet to create ledger entry (pseudo-config):
ALERT SLOBurnHigh
  IF increase(slo_burn_rate_total[5m]) > 0.05
  FOR 10m
  ANNOTATIONS {
    summary = "SLO burn >5% over 10m",
    runbook = "/confluence/eng-sre/operational-tooling/slo-ledger-and-capacity-escrow-playbook-2026"
  }
- Ledger CLI examples:
  - Create: `redwood ledger create --service text-generation-prod-v2 --slo availability_99.9 --deficit 0.25 --owner oncall-textgen --reason "tail latency after canary"`
  - Assign escrow: `redwood ledger assign-escrow --ledger-id ledg-1f3a9b --escrow-id escrow-81a2`
  - Reconcile: `redwood ledger reconcile --since 24h --output csv`

- PromQL examples to surface candidate deficits:
  - Burn rate (error-budget consumption): `sum(increase(slo_error_budget_burn_total{service="text-generation-prod-v2"}[1h]))`
  - Estimated GPU steps needed (heuristic): `ceil(sum(rate(request_tokens[5m])) / 100000)`  # heuristic placeholder

Runbook: Day-1 Play (SRE oncall)
1. Receive SLOBurnHigh or equivalent alert.
2. Pull ledger entry: `redwood ledger get --service $S --open-only` and inspect `credits_required` and `amortization_policy`.
3. Confirm current mitigation: routing fallbacks, autoscale status, and model rollbacks.
4. If automation assigned escrow, monitor applied credits and SLO trend for next 1–6h.
5. If no escrow assigned and service is degrading, request temporary escrow via: `redwood escrow request --pool safety-burst-global --credits 10 --ttl 6h --reason "oncall emergency"`
6. Document actions in incident timeline and annotate ledger entry.
7. If ledger entry approaches debt window, notify Capacity Council via #capacity-governance channel and open a formal ticket.

Runbook: Day-2 (Remediation and Retrospective)
1. After service stabilizes, run `redwood ledger reconcile --since incident-start` to summarize credit usage.
2. If amortization shortened, release unused credits back to pool: `redwood escrow release --escrow-id escrow-81a2 --credits 5`
3. Create post-incident action items: capacity sizing changes, routing policy updates, or model rollback safety checks.
4. Close ledger entry with final notes and link to postmortem.

SLO Ledger Exemptions and Edge Cases
- Planned maintenance: create pre-authorised ledger entry with `reason: maintenance` and TTL matching maintenance window.
- Blue/green deployments: use experiment-credits with TTL <= 4h.
- Customer billing disputes: tenant-escrow debit must be accompanied by an incident review and finance signoff.

Monitoring and Metrics for the Playbook
- Number of open ledger entries (gauge). Target: <= 5 open per region.
- Ledger entry age distribution. Target: median < 8h.
- Escrow utilization ratio (used/total). Target: safety-burst < 40% utilization.
- Reconciliation lag (time between amortization completed and reconciliation run). Target: < 1h.

Ownership and Contacts
- Escrow pool steward: eng-sre-capacity@redwood.ai
- Ledger service owner: runtime-platform@redwood.ai
- Capacity Council: rotation list in #capacity-governance (see related pages)

Audit and Compliance
- All ledger actions produce Kibana/ELK events and a signed record in internal audit-store.
- For enterprise customers with Dedicated/Private contracts, copy of relevant ledger events are appended to customer audit bundle.

Appendix A: Sample automation policy (policy DSL excerpt)
- match { service: "text-generation-*"; slo: "availability_*" } => { pool: "safety-burst-global"; max_credit_pct: 20; amortize: "linear-4h" }
- match { tenant: "enterprise-*" } => { pool: "tenant-escrow"; require_approval: true }

Appendix B: Troubleshooting checklist
- If automated assignment fails: check escrow pool capacity, and ledger service health (systemctl status ledger-service).
- If amortization does not apply: verify reconciliation worker logs and message queue backlog (SQS/Rabbit).
- If credits consumed but SLO remains degraded: rollback model changes or initiate multi-region failover.

Appendix C: FAQ
Q: Can teams create their own escrow pools?
A: Yes, but pools used for production SLO coverage must be registered with eng-sre-capacity and have an assigned steward.

Q: How are credits quantified?
A: Credits are an internal unit (gpu-steps, replica-hours, or region-replicas). Mapping to physical resources is defined in the pool metadata.
